rules.text: The complete system should always but always stay Tablet friendly!!
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3A: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026
rules.variant_wording: The complete system must ALWAYS remain tablet friendly.
rules.variant_source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026 §7 (a restatement, superseded by the wording below)

rules.text: We must always but always follow and amend this tracker as we go. When i feature is finished and tested and approved, then that task must be marked done on the tracker instantly. Otherwise confusion and double work will become a problem.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3A: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026
rules.variant_wording:
The tracker must ALWAYS be followed and amended as development progresses.

When a feature/task is:

- implemented
- tested
- reviewed
- approved

it must immediately be marked DONE in the tracker.

Do not leave completed work as OPEN merely because a later batch may contain related work.

This is specifically to prevent confusion and duplicate work.
rules.variant_source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026 §7 (a restatement, superseded by the wording below)

rules.text: Security is very very important from the start. we want the best of the best security models. It must always accommodate the newest and best security models. System must be hardened. Have the best of the best practices. For development phase, never touch the demo users and the way we change users to view the different roles and permissions. once development is done, we will remove that and have actual login pages with prime security etc!!!!!
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3A: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026
rules.variant_wording:
Security is extremely important from the beginning.

The system must:

- use current strong security practices
- be hardened
- follow best-practice security architecture
- accommodate improved/new security practices as the project evolves
- avoid knowingly introducing insecure shortcuts
rules.variant_source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026 §7 (a restatement, superseded by the wording below)

rules.text:
The tracker MUST NOT interfere with, modify, break, or otherwise affect the EJE application.

The EJE application is:

    VOID-za/EJE-Managment

The tracker MUST be a completely separate project.

Separate:

- Git repository
- directory
- database
- database user
- environment file
- systemd service
- application process
- logs
- configuration
- migrations
- backup strategy
- deployment
- HTTP port
- authentication
- source code

The tracker must NEVER:

- import tracker code into EJE
- modify EJE package.json
- modify EJE tsconfig
- modify EJE eslint configuration
- modify EJE Next.js configuration
- modify EJE database schema
- modify EJE database data
- modify EJE routes
- modify EJE systemd service
- modify EJE environment variables
- modify EJE Caddy configuration automatically
- modify EJE deployment scripts
- write into the EJE repository
- write into docs/SCOPE.md
- execute EJE migrations
- restart eje.service
- alter EJE users
- alter EJE demo users
- alter EJE permissions

The tracker may READ EJE documentation such as:

    docs/SCOPE.md

but must treat that information as READ-ONLY.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
This is mandatory.

Whenever functionality is changed, replaced or removed:

DO NOT simply add the new implementation.

Find and remove the old implementation where it is no longer required.

This applies to:

- code
- components
- API handlers
- domain rules
- database logic
- migrations
- schemas
- seeds
- comments
- documentation
- tests
- scripts
- feature flags
- dead branches
- obsolete helpers
- obsolete types
- obsolete imports
- obsolete CSS/UI
- old workflow paths

Do not leave:

- dead code
- duplicate implementations
- unused files
- unused functions
- obsolete comments
- contradictory documentation
- stale tests
- stale seeds
- abandoned feature branches
- unnecessary dependencies

BUT:

Never delete historical data structures that are intentionally required for audit/history compatibility.

If something appears obsolete but you cannot prove it is safe to remove:

STOP.

Record the issue in the tracker and investigate before deleting it.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Every implementation must preserve unrelated existing functionality.

A change must not accidentally break:

- existing pages
- existing routes
- existing workflows
- permissions
- customer data
- machines
- jobs
- documents
- PDFs
- signatures
- email/outbox
- delivery
- notifications
- attachments
- library
- search
- dashboards
- PostgreSQL behaviour
- seed/demo behaviour
- tablet usability

Before marking anything DONE, verify affected and relevant existing functionality.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
The database must always remain aligned with the application.

For every meaningful data-model change:

Check:

- PostgreSQL schema
- migrations
- constraints
- indexes
- foreign keys
- nullable/non-nullable fields
- enums/statuses
- seeds
- test fixtures
- application types
- API validation
- UI forms
- historical data compatibility
- PostgreSQL tests

Do not assume "no migration required" without verifying why.

If a migration is required, create and test it properly.

If no migration is required, record the reason.

The tracker database itself must follow the same standard.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
A task is NOT DONE merely because the code compiles.

Where applicable, verify:

- unit tests
- application tests
- PostgreSQL tests
- API tests
- role/permission tests
- workflow tests
- browser/e2e tests
- smoke tests
- build
- lint
- typecheck
- route checks
- tablet/viewport checks
- security implications

The tracker must record verification evidence.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
This applies to the ENTIRE EJE system.

Every new page, dialog, workflow, form and component must remain usable on tablets.

Do not treat desktop as the only target.

Where appropriate verify:

- touch targets
- no horizontal overflow
- readable text
- usable forms
- usable dialogs
- usable signatures
- usable tables
- usable workflow controls
- appropriate spacing
- tablet viewport behaviour

The tracker itself must also be tablet-friendly.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
docs/SCOPE.md remains the authoritative EJE scope document.

The tracker must NOT become a replacement for SCOPE.md.

Instead:

SCOPE.md
=
authoritative product requirement record.

Tracker
=
live project-control / implementation / status / evidence layer.

The tracker may import and display scope information.

It must never silently alter SCOPE.md.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
The tracker must distinguish clearly between:

- OPEN
- PLANNED
- IN PROGRESS
- BLOCKED
- IMPLEMENTED
- TESTING
- APPROVED
- DONE
- DEFERRED
- CANCELLED

Do NOT collapse "implemented" and "done".

A task only becomes DONE after it has been tested and approved.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
The tracker must distinguish:

- NOT STARTED
- LOCAL
- COMMITTED
- PUSHED
- DEPLOYED

Never treat PUSHED as DEPLOYED.

The live EJE build can provide deployment evidence.

Where practical, derive deployment state from:

- commit hash
- live /api/health build stamp
- git ancestry

Do not allow someone to manually claim something is deployed without evidence.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Design for future automation, but do NOT introduce dangerous automation now.

Future automation may eventually allow:

- Claude to read tracker state automatically
- Claude to update tracker after implementation
- Git commits to update tracker
- deployment health to update deployment status
- ChatGPT to query tracker state
- automatic detection of pushed-vs-deployed
- automatic detection of changed scope

BUT:

No automation may modify EJE production behaviour without explicit authorization.

No automatic deployment.

No automatic destructive action.

No automatic database mutation against EJE.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Security applies to the tracker itself.

Use strong current security practices from the beginning.

At minimum:

- authenticated access
- secure password hashing
- session security
- CSRF protection where applicable
- input validation
- authorization
- secure cookies
- security headers
- no plaintext passwords
- no secrets in Git
- no credentials in logs
- least privilege
- database user separation
- parameterized SQL
- safe error handling
- audit logging

Use current best-practice approaches rather than deliberately choosing outdated patterns.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Before declaring the tracker implementation complete:

Run its own:

- tests
- typecheck if applicable
- lint if applicable
- build
- database tests
- security checks
- API tests
- browser tests where applicable

Also verify that the EJE repository remains completely untouched.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Before finishing any tracker implementation batch:

Check the tracker repository for:

- unused files
- unused dependencies
- dead code
- duplicate implementations
- stale comments
- stale documentation
- temporary files
- debug code
- secrets
- generated junk
- unnecessary build artifacts

Do not leave scratch files behind.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
The tracker must have its own Git repository.

Every meaningful batch should have:

- implementation commit
- documentation/scope commit where appropriate
- clean working tree
- pushed branch/commit

Never claim completion with uncommitted implementation changes.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
If something is ambiguous:

STOP.

Do not decide it yourself.

Create/update a decision item and ask.

If something appears to contradict an existing rule:

STOP.

Do not silently reconcile it.

If removing something may affect history:

STOP and investigate.

If a requested change may break another feature:

STOP and investigate before implementation.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
The tracker must NEVER cause changes to the EJE application.

The tracker must also NEVER be allowed to become a dependency of the EJE application.

EJE must continue to function normally if the tracker is:

- offline
- stopped
- unavailable
- being upgraded
- being migrated
- being backed up
- completely removed

The EJE application must have ZERO runtime dependency on the tracker.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT AUTHENTICATION RULE:

During development, DO NOT change the existing demo users or the mechanism used to switch between roles/permissions.

The existing development/demo role mechanism is intentional and must remain available for testing.

After development is complete, production authentication will be implemented properly and the development/demo mechanism will be removed/replaced as part of the production-security phase.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 2: RULES + LIVE PROJECT TRACKER", 25 September 2026
